issues.body: `check_form` continues whenever `"id" not in element`, allowing input, textarea, dropdown, and checkboxes elements without IDs. The self-test then codifies that unsound behavior with four positive missing-ID cases. GitHub's issue-form syntax requires `id` on each fillable element type, so this gate can pass a structurally invalid form that GitHub rejects.
issues.fix_hint: Require an `id` key for every non-markdown element before applying the existing non-empty, character-set, and uniqueness checks. Replace the four missing-ID acceptance assertions with rejection assertions for input, textarea, dropdown, and checkboxes.
issues.title: Fillable elements still accept a missing required id

verdict.summary: The round-3 major finding remains unresolved. `check_form` still skips ID validation whenever a fillable element omits `id`, and the self-test explicitly requires all four fillable element types to pass without one. GitHub's issue-form schema requires `id` for input, textarea, dropdown, and checkboxes elements; only markdown lacks that field requirement. The added prose asserting otherwise does not make the validator sound, so the gate can approve a form GitHub rejects. Because materially the same major issue remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
